look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · An UNARMED herb with ALTERNATE simple green ovate leaves and little WHITE five-lobed flowers. Its yellow anthers are distinctly longer than those of American black nightshade (typically 1.8–2.5 mm versus ca. 0.8–1.5 mm). CONFIRM with mature fruit: S. nigrescens usually has DULL green/dark purplish berries, calyx lobes APPRESSED or spreading against the berry base, and fruit pedicels that spread or droop. S. americanum usually has shiny black berries with tiny calyx lobes STRONGLY REFLEXED backward. Do not assign species confidently from white flowers or immature fruit alone.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: Green unarmed branching herb/short-lived perennial; simple alternate ovate leaves, margins entire to shallowly toothed

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: White 5-lobed rotate/star corolla with projecting yellow relatively elongated anthers

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: Anthers generally 1.8–2.5 mm, elliptic, not almost globose short anthers as in S. americanum

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: Fruit ultimately commonly dark purplish or green/dull rather than glossy black; fruit clusters often have spreading/deflexed stalks

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: Calyx lobes below ripe berry APPRESSED to SPREADING, not strongly reflexed backwards

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: More than five hard sclerotic granules (stone cells) often in berry; specialist character, not a tasting or field-food lesson

lookalikes.differences: Hard pair: American black nightshade. Longer anthers + appressed/spreading calyx + duller fruit + spreading/deflexed pedicels favor nigrescens.
